'''John Walter Clark''' (born 1935), is [[Wayman Crow]] Professor of Physics emeritus at [[Washington University in St. Louis]], and a recipient of the [[Eugene Feenberg Memorial Medal|Eugene Feenberg Medal]] in 1987 for his contributions to [[many-body theory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://physics.wustl.edu/people/john-w-clark|title=John W. Clark|date=2018-06-19|website=Department of Physics|language=en|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

== Biography ==
John Clark was born in 1935 in [[Lockhart, Texas]]. He received his BS and MA degrees in physics from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1955 and 1957, respectively. He then earned his Ph.D. in Physics under the supervision of [[Eugene Feenberg]] at Washington University in St. Louis in 1959. He was a [[National Science Foundation Network|National Science Foundation]] Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Princeton University]] advised by [[Eugene Wigner]] and a NATO postdoctoral fellow at [[University of Birmingham]] and [[Saclay Nuclear Research Centre|Saclay]] from 1959 to 1963.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web2.ph.utexas.edu/utphysicshistory/JohnWalterClark.html|title=UTPhysicsHistorySite|website=web2.ph.utexas.edu|access-date=2019-12-28|archive-date=2019-12-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191228161310/https://web2.ph.utexas.edu/utphysicshistory/JohnWalterClark.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He named his son Eugene after his advisors.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://source.wustl.edu/2006/10/clark-searches-for-answers-to-complex-universe/|title=Clark searches for answers to 'complex universe' {{!}} The Source {{!}} Washington University in St. Louis|date=2006-10-26|website=The Source|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref> Author {{ill|Mathilde Walter Clark|da}} is his daughter.

He became an assistant professor of physics in [[Arts and Sciences at Washington University in St. Louis]] in 1963, was department chair from 2002 to 2007, and succeeded [[Edwin Thompson Jaynes|Edwin T. Jaynes]] as the Wayman Crow Professor of Physics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://libguides.wustl.edu/c.php?g=338660&p=2280777|title=Research Guides: Crow Professorship: John Walter Clark|last=Rectenwald|first=Miranda|website=libguides.wustl.edu|language=en|access-date=2019-12-28}}</ref>

== Research and teaching ==
Clark is notable for his contributions to nuclear physics and many-body theory, Later in his career, he also turned his interests to neural nets. He taught "Physics of the Brain" for many years. He supervised over two dozen Ph.D. students and was notable for promoting women in the field.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards ==

* Fellow, [[American Physical Society]]
* [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Foundation Fellowship]] (1965)
*[[:de:Feenberg-Medaille|Eugene Feenberg Medal for Many-Body Physics]] (1987)
* Wayman Crow Professorship in Physics (1999)
